attacks.claim: The weekly public CC-BY export publishes per-response rows with zip, birth_year, gender, ward, verified flag, and created_at alongside each ranking. Verified responses come from residents who gave address, zip, birth_year, and gender at verification. Removing resident_id does not stop linkage: a small poll in a small ward can single out individuals by these quasi-identifiers plus timestamp. Publication on a public open-data site is irreversible once downloaded.
attacks.evidence: "one CSV per poll on data.ourtown.org with columns ward, zip, birth_year, gender, ranking, verified, created_at. resident_id is removed before export." and "verified residents already have address, zip, birth_year, gender (collected at optional verification...)"
